title: segítenek egymásnak, számítanak egymásra: Mutual Support

sections.title: Putting egymás back to work
sections.content: Now combine the egymás case forms from Lesson 1 with two more support verbs. segít already takes a dative object (segítek neked), so its reciprocal form is segítenek egymásnak, "they help each other." számít ("to count on/matter") takes -ra/-re, so its reciprocal form is számítanak egymásra, "they count on each other." Both patterns describe support that flows both directions between two people at once.

sections.title: Reciprocal support
rows: they can count on each other
they can rely on each other

items.spanish: A jó barátok mindig segítenek egymásnak.
items.english: Good friends always help each other.
Whatever happens, we can count on each other.
In a hard situation we learned to rely on each other.

sections.content: számít changes meaning slightly depending on what follows it: számít valakire is "to count on someone," but számít alone (without a case-marked object) often just means "it matters" — Ez nem számít, "this doesn't matter." Keep the case attached in your head as part of the meaning, not as an optional extra.
